According to CPMAI methodology, which of the following represents the most effective use of generative AI to accelerate this chatbot project timeline?
options: Using generative AI to completely replace human developers in coding the chatbot, eliminating the need for a development team
Using generative AI creates synthetic customer service conversations for training, response templates, and code assistance, while humans ensure quality and appropriateness.
Using generative AI to automatically determine the project scope and requirements without stakeholder input, saving time in the Business Understanding phase.
Using generative AI to generate the final production chatbot directly from the project requirements document, skipping the Data Understanding and Data Preparation phases.

questions.question:
A financial services company is developing a credit scoring model. The data science team is discussing whether to use a single algorithm or an ensemble approach.
Which of the following most accurately describes how ensemble methods can improve model performance for this credit scoring application?
options: Ensemble methods combine multiple identical algorithms trained on the same data to reduce the need for feature engineering
Ensemble methods combine predictions from multiple diverse models to reduce variance, bias, or both, potentially improving accuracy and robustness beyond what any single model could achieve
Ensemble methods use a sequence of increasingly complex models, with each model in the sequence handling more difficult cases than the previous one
Ensemble methods automatically select the single best algorithm from a collection of algorithms based on validation performance

questions.question:
A legal tech company is implementing prompt engineering techniques to improve their legal document analysis system based on a large language model (LLM). The team is discussing different prompt engineering approaches.
Which of the following represents the most effective prompt engineering technique for improving the accuracy and relevance of LLM responses in specialized legal document analysis?
options: Using chain-of-thought prompting that guides the model through a step-by-step reasoning process, combined with few-shot examples of desired analysis patterns and explicit instructions about legal constraints and requirements
Providing zero-shot prompts with minimal context to test the model’s generalization ability while ensuring it avoids legal terminology.
Embedding legal documents directly into the prompt and asking the model to summarize them using standard reasoning heuristics.
Using a single-shot example that demonstrates ideal output structure, assuming the model will generalize the reasoning and comply with applicable rules.

questions.question:

Neural networks learn features by flattening input data into uniform layers, relying on rule-based filters to extract key patterns.
Neural networks learn complex features from raw data automatically through layered abstractions, without manual engineering.

Decision trees

Artificial General Intelligence

Project professional
Cybersecurity expert

Prioritize velocity and revisit explainability after pilot testing.

questions.question:

Reliability checks
Context detailing

questions.question:

Increasing model layers

Underfitting
Prediction bias
Lack of real-time data

Recognition
Hyper-Personalization
Autonomous Systems

What algorithmic strategy is most appropriate?
options: Clustering with K-means and heuristics
Naive Bayes Classifier
Support Vector Machine ensemble
Pretrained Transformer Model with Fine-tuning

Proceed with existing data and fine-tune the model post-deployment.
Partner with local firms to collect region-specific data.
Apply hyper-personalization to adjust outputs during inference.
options: 1 only

questions.question: After initial testing, your model performs well on historical data but poorly on recent events involving new suppliers. Some team members argue this reflects model limitations, while others suggest revisiting earlier data assumptions. How should the team proceed under CPMAI?
options: Reevaluate data selection and assumptions made in Phase 2.
Adjust thresholds to force-fit outputs to business expectations.
Proceed with deployment and retrain post-launch using new events.
Attribute variance to market anomalies and monitor post-deployment.

How can this issue best be resolved?
options: Use supervised learning
Implement RAG
Increase training epochs
Adopt reinforcement learning

questions.question: A project manager is tasked with selecting an AI approach for a financial institution aiming to automate loan approval processes. options: Goal-driven systems with optimization for cost-benefit trade-offs in loan decisions.
Pattern and anomaly detection with emphasis on real-time data integration for dynamic approvals.
Conversational AI with robust natural language processing to handle applicant queries.
Predictive analytics with a focus on feature engineering to ensure model interpretability.

questions.question:

options: Misinformation
Disinformation
Hallucination
Manipulation

questions.question:

Which limitation is most responsible for this failure?
options: Static training data
Lack of explainability
High variability
Automation

questions.question:

Before diving into data or technical development, leadership wants to estimate potential ROI and identify the right team to execute the project. Which CPMAI phase addresses ROI estimation and team assembly?
options: Data Understanding
Business Understanding
Model Development
Deployment

questions.question:

options: Accountability
Transparency
Privacy
Fairness

questions.question: A healthcare project involves predicting patient readmission risk using electronic health records (EHRs). options: Deep Neural Network

Decision Tree
Transformer Model

questions.question:
A telecommunications company is implementing an AI system to predict network equipment failures before they occur. The model performs well in testing, but the operations team is concerned about how to integrate it with existing network monitoring systems and maintenance workflows.
According to the CPMAI Model Operationalization phase, which integration approach would most effectively ensure operational adoption and value realization?
options: Deploy the AI system as a standalone platform with its own dashboard and alerting system, requiring network operations staff to monitor both existing systems and the new AI platform.
Fully automate the maintenance dispatch process based on AI predictions, eliminating the need for human review to maximize efficiency gains.

Integrate the AI predictions into existing monitoring dashboards with clear confidence scores, establish tiered alert protocols based on failure probability, and create streamlined workflows for maintenance prioritization.
Implement the AI system in parallel with existing processes for six months, requiring duplicate work from operations teams to validate the AI predictions against current methods.

questions.question:
A project manager is tasked with designing an AI-powered customer support system that must handle multilingual queries across multiple channels. The goal is to provide natural, real-time interaction while identifying customer intent and issues accurately. To achieve this, the manager must choose a combination of AI patterns that support both understanding and effective communication. Selecting the right pair will ensure the system delivers timely, context-aware support in various languages.
Which  AI patterns combine most effectively for this use case?
options: Conversational + Predictive Analytics + Hyper personalization
Conversational + Goal driven + Hyper personalization
Conversational + Pattern detection
Conversational + Generative AI

questions.question:
A project manager uses a Generative AI tool to draft a project charter, hoping to streamline the creation of key project documentation. Upon reviewing the document, they notice that several sections are identical to content found in previous publications, including proprietary reports from other companies. Concerned about the legal and ethical implications, the project manager investigates further and realizes that the AI tool has inadvertently reproduced copyrighted material without proper attribution. This raises alarms within the organization regarding the potential misuse of intellectual property and the reputational risk it poses. The project manager must determine which type of risk the company faces due to this issue.
Which risk is most evident in this scenario?
options: IP misappropriation
Data bias
Prompt injection
Model drift

questions.question: After deployment, the model begins to exhibit drift as suppliers change their fulfillment policies. Your team receives complaints that forecasts are outdated and missing new behavior patterns. There’s no retraining schedule in place, and stakeholder trust is declining. What action is most aligned with CPMAI?
options: Increase model complexity to compensate for drift.
Implement a monitoring dashboard and retrain pipeline based on trigger thresholds.
Decommission the AI model and return to manual forecasting.
Freeze the model and rely on business rules until drift is resolved.

questions.question:

Which technique should the team use to address this?
options: Early stopping
Regularization
Data augmentation
Feature selection

questions.question:

Upon investigation, it becomes clear that the project was hampered by unreliable or poorly validated sensor data, which led to erroneous model predictions. The project team realizes they overlooked the importance of understanding and validating the data at the early stages. They refer back to the CPMAI methodology to identify which phase should have addressed these issues.
Which CPMAI methodology phase was likely inadequate in this scenario?
options: Model Development
Business Understanding
Data Understanding
Data Operationalization

questions.question:

A/B testing
Cross-validation

questions.question: A multinational corporation is deploying an AI system to optimize global supply chain logistics, requiring integration of autonomous systems for warehouse robots and predictive analytics for demand forecasting. options: Combine autonomous systems and predictive analytics, prioritizing real-time data pipelines and continuous model retraining to handle dynamic supply chain demands.
Integrate goal-driven systems and hyper-personalization, focusing on optimizing resource allocation and tailoring logistics to regional customer preferences.
Merge pattern and anomaly detection with conversational AI, emphasizing anomaly detection in logistics data and chatbot interfaces for stakeholder communication.
Blend recognition and predictive analytics, leveraging computer vision for warehouse operations and statistical models for demand prediction.

questions.question: A healthcare organization is deploying an AI system for patient triage, combining predictive analytics for risk scoring and conversational AI for patient interaction. The system must comply with HIPAA, mitigate risks of deepfakes in patient video consultations, and address bias in historical medical data, as emphasized in both CPMAI and AI Essentials. Which strategy best ensures trustworthiness, regulatory compliance, and ethical AI deployment?
options: Combine ensemble methods for bias reduction, implement anomaly detection for deepfake identification, and rely on third-party audits for HIPAA compliance.
Use explainable AI models with LIME for transparency, deploy audio-visual synchronization checks for deepfakes, and apply data anonymization for HIPAA compliance.
Fine-tune the AI system with synthetic patient data to avoid bias, use forensic pixel analysis for deepfake detection, and encrypt data for HIPAA compliance.
Implement a bias mitigation framework with fairness-aware algorithms, integrate deepfake detection tools, and establish a HIPAA-compliant data life cycle with regular audits.

questions.question:
During the Model Development phase of an AI project, an AI engineer suggests using a deep learning model for real-time project risk prediction, believing it will deliver higher accuracy. However, the project sponsor is concerned about the lack of explainability in deep learning models, which could affect decision-making and stakeholder trust. They argue for the use of simpler decision trees, which are more interpretable. The project manager, referencing PMI's guidelines, seeks a solution that balances technical performance with ethical concerns, ensuring the model’s accuracy while maintaining transparency.
Which CPMAI-recommended approach resolves this conflict?
options: Use a neural network but add SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) for interpretability.
Prioritize explainability by adopting decision trees despite lower accuracy.
Implement a hybrid model combining both techniques with HITL validation.
Delay deployment until a fully explainable deep learning framework is available.

questions.question:

Upon conducting audits, the team discovers that the model’s training data does not include recent stakeholder feedback, which is crucial for understanding evolving team dynamics. options: Retrain the model using updated stakeholder data and enforce HITL validation for high-stakes decisions.
Replace the AI system with a rules-based engine preconfigured to the original risk matrix.
Implement RAG to dynamically integrate real-time stakeholder sentiment analysis and audit logs.
Reduce the model’s prediction frequency to minimize exposure to evolving data patterns.

questions.question:
During the Problem Identification phase of an AI-driven supply chain project, the team faces disagreement among stakeholders regarding whether to prioritize cost reduction or risk mitigation. The project manager looks to PMI’s guidance for defining clear and aligned objectives that consider both business goals and stakeholder input. The aim is to ensure the AI system delivers measurable value while addressing organizational needs.
Which two actions align with PMI’s guidance for defining objectives?
Conduct a cross-functional workshop to map AI capabilities to organizational KPIs.
Use predictive analytics to quantify the ROI of both priorities.
Draft a project charter excluding ethical considerations to avoid delays.
Align the AI system’s goal-driven pattern with the most vocal stakeholder’s preference.

questions.question: A project team is developing a real-time fraud detection system for a global e-commerce platform. The data is highly imbalanced, with fewer positive fraud cases. options: Naive Bayes
K-means Clustering
LSTM Neural Network
Random Forest with SHAP integration

questions.question:

The CIO wants to accelerate implementation by focusing on a single, standardized AI model for all facilities.
According to the CPMAI methodology, which approach would most effectively balance the CIO's desire for standardization with the data heterogeneity challenges?
options: Proceed with a single model approach but extend the Data Preparation phase to transform all facility data into a standardized format, accepting potential information loss.
Implement a federated learning approach where local models are trained on facility-specific data while contributing to a global model that captures common patterns.
Develop a modular AI architecture with a core prediction engine and facility specific data transformation layers that normalize inputs while preserving local operational nuances.
Recommend postponing the project until a global data standardization initiative can be implemented across all manufacturing facilities.

questions.question:
A financial services organization is developing an AI system to detect potential fraud in loan applications. The organization operates in a heavily regulated industry where loan decisions must be justifiable to both customers and regulators.
According to CPMAI principles for Model Development and trustworthy AI, which consideration should be the primary driver for this decision?
options: Prioritize the deep learning model's accuracy, but implement post-hoc explainability techniques like SHAP or LIME to approximate explanations for individual predictions.
Select the explainable ensemble model, as regulatory compliance and customer trust requirements outweigh the marginal accuracy improvement of the black-box approach.
Implement both models in parallel: use the deep learning model for initial screening and the explainable model for final decisions that require justification.
Develop a hybrid approach that incorporates the most important features identified by the explainable model into a constrained deep learning architecture with inherent interpretability.

questions.question:
A healthcare organization is implementing an AI system to predict patient deterioration in hospital wards. The project has completed the first five phases of CPMAI and is now in the Model Operationalization phase. The model performs well in controlled testing, but the team must decide how to integrate it with existing clinical workflows and electronic health record (EHR) systems.
According to the CPMAI Model Operationalization phase, which deployment approach would most effectively ensure clinical adoption and patient safety?
options: Deploy the model as a standalone alert system that operates independently of the EHR, sending notifications to clinical staff when deterioration risk is high.
Fully integrate the model within the EHR system, automatically triggering clinical protocols based on risk scores without requiring clinician review.

Implement a tiered deployment approach with progressive clinical involvement: silent monitoring phase, advisory alerts requiring clinician acknowledgment, and finally measured protocol suggestions with clear override options.
Deploy the model as an on-demand tool that clinicians can choose to consult when they have concerns about a patient, preserving complete clinical autonomy.

options: Combine autonomous systems and predictive analytics, prioritizing real-time data pipelines and continuous model retraining to handle dynamic supply chain demands.

Blend recognition and predictive analytics, leveraging computer vision for warehouse operations and statistical models for demand prediction.

questions.question: A project team is designing a data architecture for an AI-driven project management platform that integrates real-time stakeholder feedback (unstructured text) and historical project performance data (structured). The platform must support predictive analytics for risk assessment and generative AI for report generation, while addressing data privacy concerns under GDPR and ensuring data quality to avoid “garbage in, garbage out.” Which data engineering approach best supports these requirements?
options: Design a hybrid data pipeline with separate batch and streaming workflows, incorporating NLP for text preprocessing, differential privacy for GDPR compliance, and automated data quality checks.
Implement a unified data lake with cloud-based storage, using tokenization for GDPR compliance and unsupervised clustering for data quality assessment.
Develop a streaming-only pipeline with real-time NLP processing, applying data anonymization for GDPR and manual data validation for quality control.

questions.question:
A retail company is developing an AI-powered inventory management system using the Predictive Analytics pattern. During the Data Understanding phase, they discover that while they have extensive historical sales data, there are significant gaps in their inventory records due to periodic system migrations and inconsistent stocktaking procedures. The project sponsor is concerned about how these data quality issues will impact the project.
According to the CPMAI methodology's approach to data challenges, which strategy would most effectively address this situation?
options: Proceed with model development using only the sales data, focusing on demand forecasting rather than comprehensive inventory management.
Implement a data quality remediation project as a prerequisite to the AI initiative, delaying the project until complete inventory records are available.
Develop a hybrid approach that uses available high-quality data for initial model development while simultaneously implementing processes to improve data collection for future iterations.
Abandon the AI approach and implement a rule-based inventory management system that is less dependent on historical data quality.

questions.question:

Stakeholders are divided on whether to proceed with deployment.

options: Conduct extensive simulation testing with synthetic edge cases to stress-test the model's decision boundaries before deployment.
Implement A/B testing by deploying the model to a small segment of the grid and comparing performance to traditional control methods.
Perform sensitivity analysis to understand how the model responds to various input parameters and environmental conditions in the simulation environment.

Establish a comprehensive evaluation framework that includes technical performance metrics, business KPIs, safety considerations, and a phased real-world validation plan with increasing levels of model autonomy.

questions.question:
A transportation company is implementing an AI system to optimize route planning and logistics. According to CPMAI best practices for multi-pattern AI implementations, which data preparation approach would be most effective?
options: Create separate data pipelines for each AI pattern, optimizing each for its specific requirements without concern for integration points.
Prioritize the Predictive Analytics pattern as the foundation and structure all data preparation to support its needs, with other patterns as secondary considerations.
Develop a unified data architecture with a common core dataset and pattern-specific preprocessing modules, ensuring consistent feature definitions across all components.
Outsource the data preparation to specialized vendors for each pattern, then integrate their outputs through a custom middleware layer.

questions.question:

During the Business Understanding phase, they identify that the system will need to process sensitive demographic data while ensuring fairness across different population segments. According to CPMAI principles for trustworthy AI, at which points in the project lifecycle should ethical considerations be addressed?
options: During the Business Understanding phase to establish ethical guidelines, and again during Model Evaluation to verify compliance.
Primarily during the Data Understanding and Data Preparation phases to ensure representative and unbiased training data.
During Model Development when selecting algorithms with appropriate fairness constraints and explainability features.
Throughout all six phases of CPMAI, with specific ethical considerations embedded in each phase from business understanding through operationalization.

questions.question:

options: Exclude demographic variables from the model entirely to ensure the AI doesn't perpetuate historical patterns, focusing only on transaction history and account behavior.
Proceed with model development using all variables but implement postprocessing fairness corrections that ensure equal recommendation rates across demographic groups.

Analyze the root causes of the different adoption patterns, distinguish between appropriate personalization and problematic bias, and implement targeted bias mitigation techniques while preserving legitimate behavioral signals.
Create separate models for each demographic group to ensure optimal recommendations within each population segment.

questions.question:
An organization is implementing an AI-powered document processing system using the Recognition pattern to extract information from various document types. During the Model Development phase, they must decide between using a pre-trained foundation model with fine-tuning or developing a custom model from scratch. According to CPMAI best practices for Model Development, which approach would most effectively balance development efficiency with performance requirements?
options: Implement a transfer learning approach using a pre-trained foundation model with extensive fine-tuning on the domain-specific labeled data, evaluating performance against business requirements.
Use a pre-trained foundation model with minimal fine-tuning to maximize development speed, accepting potential performance limitations.
Develop a custom model from scratch to ensure optimal performance for the specific document types and extraction requirements.
Create an ensemble that combines multiple pre-trained models without fine-tuning, using a voting mechanism to determine the final extraction results.

questions.question:

The project team has completed the Business Understanding phase and identified that the system will need to predict inventory needs, detect supply disruptions, and autonomously adjust procurement schedules. During the Data Understanding phase, they discover that while they have extensive historical data, regional offices use different data schemas, and real-time data integration has significant latency issues.
According to the CPMAI methodology, which combination of factors presents the most critical risk to this project's success?
options: The project combines multiple AI patterns (Predictive Analytics, Pattern & Anomaly Detection, and Autonomous Systems) without clear prioritization of which pattern should drive the data architecture.

The data integration latency issues will prevent the Autonomous Systems pattern from functioning effectively, while the inconsistent data schemas will compromise the Pattern & Anomaly Detection capabilities.
The Business Understanding phase was likely incomplete since it didn't identify the data schema inconsistencies that should have been addressed before proceeding to Data Understanding.
The project scope encompasses too many AI patterns simultaneously, and should be restructured to focus exclusively on Predictive Analytics before expanding to other patterns.

questions.question:

options: Deploy the model but implement enhanced human review processes for transactions from the affected international regions until more labeled data can be collected.
Delay deployment and use synthetic data generation techniques to augment the training data for underrepresented regions before retraining the model.
Proceed with deployment but establish a comprehensive monitoring system specifically focused on the model's performance in the affected regions.
Recommend a "No-Go" decision for deployment until the model can be retrained with a more balanced dataset that reduces bias against the affected regions.

questions.question:

The buildings have varying IoT sensor infrastructures, and the model will need to adapt to seasonal changes in energy usage patterns.

questions.question: CPMAI Methodology Overview
options: What it is: CPMAI is a vendor-neutral, iterative, and data-centric framework designed specifically for managing Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) projects successfully.

Why it's needed: Traditional project management and application development methodologies often fail to address the complexities unique to AI projects, which are data-driven rather than just software-driven. AI projects face a high failure rate, often exceeding 80%, due to issues like poor project management, misaligned business objectives, and inadequate data preparation. CPMAI integrates AI-specific principles to address these challenges.

How it addresses challenges: CPMAI mitigates risks by ensuring business alignment, data feasibility, real-world AI system evaluation and operationalisation, and iterative development. It focuses on specific requirements like alignment with business objectives and ROI, proper data preparation and governance, robust model evaluation and operationalisation, and iterative development.

Value Proposition: CPMAI extends proven approaches like agile and data-focused frameworks with AI-specific best practices. Its benefits include an iterative, data-centric focus woven into every step, structured feasibility checks (AI Go/No-Go process looking at business, data, and implementation feasibility), integration with existing organisational practices, ongoing model monitoring and governance (MLOps), and a focus on real-world ROI and trustworthiness

questions.question: Addressing the High Rate of Failure of AI Projects
options: Context: Most AI initiatives do not meet expectations, with 80% or more failing to deliver impact or move beyond prototypes. These failures are primarily due to planning, management, and alignment issues, not the AI technology itself.
◦Common Pitfalls:
▪Lack of clear business alignment: Projects start without specific ROI goals, success metrics, or stakeholder buy-in, failing to solve a pressing need.
▪Neglecting data feasibility: Teams proceed without validating data quantity and quality, leading to underperforming or flawed systems.
▪No plan for continuous updates: AI models require ongoing maintenance as data and environments shift; treating AI as a one-time project leads to performance degradation (model or data drift).

Challenges with Traditional Approaches: Traditional methods fall short because AI projects are highly data-driven, require iterative rechecking of data and models (not just features), need continuous monitoring and updates post-deployment (MLOps), and older data-analytics methods like CRISP-DM lack features for modern AI challenges such as governance, explainability, and trust.

questions.question: Generative AI (GenAI): A subset of AI focused on the creation of new content based on learned patterns. Popular GenAI solutions are Large Language Models (LLMs). GenAI models are often specific to the type of content they generate (text, images).
options: GenAI Foundation Models: Large, pretrained models for general domains like language or computer vision. They can be a starting base for building AI systems, reducing time and costs. They are trained on massive amounts of unlabeled data and can perform multiple tasks. They can be adapted or fine-tuned for specific tasks.

Large Language Models (LLMs): Trained foundation models that use deep learning neural networks (specifically transformer models) to generate human-understandable text from prompts. They understand, summarize, generate, and predict content using large data sets. Uses include text generation, summarization, translation, search, Q&A, classification, code generation, and art generation.

Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT) Models: Foundation models that use transformer models to turn prompts into text, image, audio, or other content. They are effective at transforming one sequence into another. Examples include ChatGPT, Copilot, and Llama.

questions.question:
Predictive AI: An AI system that makes predictions or recommendations based on historical data. It addresses problems like classification, forecasting, anomaly detection, clustering, and time series analysis.
How Predictive AI Works: Uses historical data to predict future outcomes, with more data generally leading to greater accuracy. Clean data is important. Techniques include:
options: Regression analysis: Studies relationships between variables.
Decision trees: Categorizes data based on variables, resembling a tree structure. Best for understanding individual decisions.
Neural networks: Used for complex predictive relationships and pattern recognition, can also validate results.

questions.question: Phase I: Business Understanding The first phase focuses on understanding the project objectives and requirements from a business perspective and converting this knowledge into an AI project problem definition and a preliminary plan. It establishes the foundation for an AI project by defining the business problem, setting success metrics, and clarifying scope. The Generic Tasks for this phase include:
options: Determine Business Objectives: Understand what the customer wants to accomplish from a business perspective in a manner consistent with cognitive technology goals, balancing competing objectives and constraints. This involves pinpointing the true need, defining clear, measurable success criteria, and performing cost/benefit analysis.
Assess Situation: Conduct detailed fact-finding about the resources, constraints, assumptions, schedule, timing, and dependency requirements relevant to the cognitive task.
Cognitive Project Requirements: Identify the relevant pattern(s) of AI for the project. This task group also includes cognitive requirements, transparency requirements, and acceptable metrics.

AI Go/No-Go: Determine whether you can proceed with a cognitive project based on a clear problem description relative to the business objectives. This involves assessing business feasibility, data feasibility, and execution feasibility.
Produce Project Plan: Describe the intended plan for achieving the cognitive and business goals, specifying stages, duration, resources, inputs, outputs, and dependencies.

questions.question: Phase II: Data Understanding This phase focuses on data needs identification, initial data collection, data requirements, data quality identification, and gaining insights into the data. It's where potential pitfalls like lack of data, privacy concerns, or data ownership uncertainty can first be exposed. The Generic Tasks for this phase include:
options: Collect Initial Data: Collect data to understand what data is available and its various formats.
Describe Data: Understand data source formats, identify training data, test data, and edge model needs.
Explore Data: Perform data exploration activities.
Verify Data Quality: Verify data quality, as addressing data quality issues early prevents downstream problems.
Pretrained Models: Task related to the usage of pre-trained and third-party models.

questions.question: Phase III: Data Preparation This phase is focused on getting the required data into a form and shape that can be used for modeling purposes. It often consumes a significant portion of project time. The Generic Tasks for this phase include:
options: Data Selection: Selecting the data.
Data Cleansing & Enhancement: Cleaning and enhancing/augmenting the data. This involves addressing data quality problems identified earlier.
Data Labeling: Labeling the data.

questions.question: Phase IV: Model Development In this phase, the project team creates and iterates on the model based on the identified and prepared data. This involves selecting the right tools and algorithms, training and tuning the model, and systematically tracking experiments. The Generic Tasks for this phase include:
options: Select Modeling Technique: Select cognitive-relevant algorithms/modeling techniques, consider ensemble methods, AutoML usage, fine-tuning/re-training of pre-trained models, and usage of Generative AI.
Model Test and Validation Design: Generate the model test design.
Model Training / Model Building: Train and build the model.
Hyperparameter Optimization: Tasks focused on maximizing fit and other model-related measures, such as fine-tuning key parameters.

questions.question: Phase V: Model Evaluation Once a model is created, this phase evaluates it to ensure it performs according to the business requirements and other factors set in Phase I. It involves assessing technical and business performance. The Generic Tasks for this phase include:
options: Evaluate model results: Measure and evaluate the model against Phase I objectives. This includes performing technical performance metrics like accuracy, precision, and recall and measuring model performance against required business KPIs and technology KPIs.
Model Iteration Approach: Determine the steps needed if the model does not perform adequately, outlining the iteration approach.
Review process: Summarize the process review and highlight activities that may have been missed or should be repeated. Detail required approvals or reviews before the model can be operationalised.

questions.question: Phase VI: Model Operationalization The final phase involves successfully deploying and using the validated AI solution in a production environment. It goes beyond simple deployment to address continuous integration, monitoring, governance, and user adoption. The Generic Tasks for this phase include:
options: Model operationalization plan: Develop a plan for putting the model into operation, determining deployment environments, and addressing any required non-AI/non-cognitive activities.

Model monitoring and maintenance: Establish a plan for continuous monitoring and maintenance, including real-time monitoring, versioning and retraining pipelines, and defining a Model Governance Framework.

Determine Requirements for the Next Iteration: Decide how to proceed based on the results of the assessment and process review, determining what the next iteration should require and considering available resources.
Project Report: Produce a final project report and review the project.
Once Phase VI is complete for the first iteration, the CPMAI process circles back to Phase I, beginning the next iteration for continuous improvement

questions.question:
Trustworthy AI
Purpose: Ensure AI solutions are built and deployed in a way that inspires confidence and mitigates risk, aligning with organizational and societal values. Integrating this with CPMAI helps reduce harm, reputational damage, and compliance violations while fostering trust.
Core Principles:
options: Ethical AI: Avoid harm, respect privacy, use data responsibly, align decisions with values.
Responsible AI: Maintain accountability for outcomes; define a human chain of accountability.
Transparent AI: Provide insight into AI behaviour, data use, and decision logic; minimise 'black boxes'; ensure visibility into processes, data configuration, bias mitigation, and consent.
Governed AI: Enforce policies for oversight (audits, compliance); includes data governance, model versioning, approval processes.
Explainable AI: Provide understandable rationale for model outputs, even for complex algorithms, using interpretability layers.

Decision-Making: Reducing delays and uncertainty by analyzing factors using autonomous systems, predictive analytics, and pattern/anomaly detection. GenAI integration requires ethical and security evaluation. Applications include data-driven decision-making (analyzing vast data for insights), automated testing (predicting issues and executing test scenarios), and analyzing project trends (finding trends and anomalies in historical data).

Project Monitoring: Providing reports and overviews to ensure projects meet milestones. AI-assisted monitoring is leaner and more efficient. Applications include project reports (automating generation and status updates), project tracking (tracking data in real-time for live reports), and project health statistics (visualizing key metrics).

Communication and Collaboration: Facilitating communication by generating updates, reports, and tailored messages. Applications include automating communications (chatbots, data distribution), note-taking and dictation (transcribing, organizing, searching meeting notes), aggregating information (organizing and distributing project info), and automated to-do lists and reminders (triggering reminders based on events).

Document Management: Monitoring, identifying needs, and creating project documentation. Applications include identifying documentation needs (reviewing code/details to determine needed content) and analyzing key insights from documentation (reviewing metrics like page views).

Cost Management: Assisting in monitoring expenses and optimizing budgets. Applications include budget optimization (analyzing financial data and external factors), cost-benefit analysis (generating first drafts using predictive analysis and pattern recognition), and cost planning (reviewing historical data and providing predictions).
